title: Gregor Mendel's birth chart
metaDescription: Gregor Mendel's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.1° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.6° separates Mars and Neptune from an exact square; at that range drive and imagination read as one mechanism. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 27.1° Cancer — deep enough in the third decan (20°–30°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 17.6° Cancer; Venus stands at 19.3° Gemini; Mars stands at 2.7° Libra. The tradition reads thought steeped in tone and memory from Mercury, attraction that begins as conversation from Venus, effort aimed through strategy and words from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars at right angles from Neptune, 0.6° off exact. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Pluto at 0.9°, and Uranus conjunction Neptune at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Pluto while both square Uranus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, one placement stands out. Mars in Libra at 2.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in earth, 2 in water, 2 in fire, 2 in air by element, 6 cardinal, 2 fixed, 1 mutable by modality. Jupiter crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day, so its sign is left open. Mercury, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.8° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 21.8°.
